ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, on a rough horizontal tabletop, one end of a light string of length l=0.2 m is tied to a small ball of mass m=1kg, and the hand holds the other end O of the light string and makes uniform circular motion in the horizontal plane; the small ball also makes uniform circular motion with the motion of the hand. The light string always remains horizontal with the tabletop. The radius of the circular motion made by point O is r=0.15 m, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the small ball and the tabletop is μ=0.3, and take g=10 m/s2. When the light string is tangent to the trajectory of the circular motion made by point O, which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The linear velocity of the small ball doing circular motion is 1 m/s

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, two concentric dashed circles can be seen. Point O is located on the inner dashed circle, and the dashed radius from the circle center to O is marked r; the small ball is on the outer dashed circle, and point O and the small ball are connected by a segment of light string marked l. In the figure, the light string is tangent at point O to the circular trajectory of point O, so the radius r from the circle center to O is perpendicular to the light string l, and the radius of the small ball making circular motion around the same circle center is R=√(r^2+l^2). Substituting r=0.15 m and l=0.20 m gives R=√(0.15^2+0.20^2)=0.25 m. The small ball is acted on in the horizontal direction by the string tension T and the kinetic friction force f exerted on it by the tabletop. Because the light string is horizontal, the vertical support force N=mg, so f=μmg=0.3×1×10=3 N. The small ball makes uniform circular motion, and the tangential resultant force is zero; the tension is along the direction of the string, and its component in the tangential direction of the small ball's circular motion is T·r/R, so T·r/R=f. Thus T=fR/r=3×0.25/0.15=5 N. In the radial direction, the radial component of the tension is T·l/R, providing the centripetal force: m v^2/R=T·l/R. Multiplying both sides by R gives m v^2=T l, so v^2=Tl/m=5×0.20/1=1, therefore v=1 m/s.
